983324335.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The superior/dorsal surface of the tongue displaying the terminal sulcus (sulcus terminalis) dividing it into the anterior two-thirds (oral part covered with filiform, fungiform, and vallate papillae) and the posterior one-third (pharyngeal part containing lingual tonsils).
983324335.keyConcept: Dorsum of tongue: Divided by the V-shaped sulcus terminalis into anterior 2/3 (presulcal, papillae-bearing) and posterior 1/3 (postsulcal, lymphoid follicles).

1943382083.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large fan-shaped extrinsic tongue muscle originating from the superior mental spine (genial tubercle) of the mandible and inserting into the body of the hyoid bone and along the entire length of the tongue from root to tip; acts to protrude and depress the tongue.
1943382083.keyConcept: Genioglossus muscle: The 'safety muscle' of the tongue; innervated by CN XII (hypoglossal nerve), its bilateral contraction protrudes the tongue.

1652532226.explanation: Criteria of Identification: U-shaped bone in the anterior neck at the C3 level, situated between the floor of the mouth and the thyroid cartilage; serves as an attachment site for suprahyoid and infrahyoid muscles and the base of the tongue.
1652532226.keyConcept: Hyoid bone: Suspended bone of the anterior neck that does not articulate with any other bone; supports the tongue and anchors laryngeal muscles.

188312730.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Conical, muscular projection hanging down in the midline from the free posterior border of the soft palate; contains the musculus uvulae and assists in closing off the nasopharynx during swallowing.
188312730.keyConcept: Uvula: Muscular midline projection of the soft palate; innervated by the pharyngeal plexus (CN X), deviation indicates vagal nerve lesion (deviates away from affected side).

228622574.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Rigid bony partition forming the anterior two-thirds of the palate and roof of the oral cavity, formed by the palatine processes of the maxillae anteriorly and horizontal plates of the palatine bones posteriorly.
228622574.keyConcept: Hard palate: Bony roof of the mouth and floor of the nasal cavities; covered by keratinized stratified squamous epithelium bound firmly to periosteum.

1696153053.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Mobile, fibromuscular fold suspended from the posterior margin of the hard palate, extending posteroinferiorly into the pharynx to separate the nasopharynx from the oropharynx during swallowing.
1696153053.keyConcept: Soft palate: Movable muscular fold consisting of muscle fibers, aponeurosis, lymphoid tissue, and mucous glands; elevated by tensor and levator veli palatini to seal the nasopharynx.

925146812.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Thick, dense bone forming the lower jaw; the sagittal section demonstrates the symphysis menti and alveolar process supporting the lower dentition, providing inner attachment for the genial tubercles.
925146812.keyConcept: Mandible: Single lower facial bone articulating with the temporal bones at the TMJ; bears the lower teeth and anchors suprahyoid and masticatory muscles.

390105954.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Paired facial bone forming the upper jaw; sagittal cross-section shows the alveolar process housing the maxillary incisors and palatine process contributing to the anterior hard palate.
390105954.keyConcept: Maxilla: Major bone of the upper face; forms parts of the floor of the orbits, lateral walls and floor of the nasal cavity, and the upper dental arch.

597116401.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Fleshy muscular fold bounding the oral fissure superiorly, extending inferiorly from the base of the nose; contains the orbicularis oris muscle, labial glands, and is lined externally by skin and internally by mucous membrane.
597116401.keyConcept: Upper lip: Musculocutaneous upper boundary of the oral fissure; innervated sensory by the infraorbital nerve (V2) and motor by facial nerve (CN VII).

917115637.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Fleshy muscular fold bounding the oral fissure inferiorly, separated from the chin by the labiomental sulcus; contains orbicularis oris muscle, covered by skin externally and non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium internally.
917115637.keyConcept: Lower lip: Inferior boundary of the oral fissure; innervated sensory by the mental nerve (branch of inferior alveolar nerve from V3) and motor by the facial nerve (CN VII).

1897019984.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Tag 1 indicates the inner lip of the ventral segment (anterior two-thirds) of the iliac crest. The muscle originating from the inner lip of the iliac crest (as well as the lateral one-third of the inguinal ligament, thoracolumbar fascia, and lower 6 costal cartilages) is the transversus abdominis muscle.
1897019984.keyConcept: Transversus abdominis: Deepest flat abdominal muscle; originates from the inner lip of the iliac crest, lower six costal cartilages, thoracolumbar fascia, and lateral inguinal ligament.

371829878.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Slit-like space of the oral cavity situated between the lips and cheeks externally, and the dental arches and gingivae internally; communicates with the exterior through the oral fissure (rima oris).
371829878.keyConcept: Oral vestibule (mouth vestibule): Peripheral space of the mouth outside the teeth; receives secretions from the parotid duct opposite the upper second molar tooth.

1373329911.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The circled middle subdivision of the pharynx, extending from the soft palate above to the superior border of the epiglottis below; communicates anteriorly with the oral cavity through the oropharyngeal isthmus and houses the palatine tonsils within the tonsillar sinuses.
1373329911.keyConcept: Oropharynx: Middle pharyngeal compartment (C2–C3 level); common passage for food and air, lined by non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium and innervated sensory by CN IX.

1841975671.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The circled superior division of the pharynx, located posterior to the nasal cavities (choanae) and superior to the soft palate; contains the pharyngeal tonsils in its roof and the lateral pharyngeal openings of the auditory (Eustachian) tubes.
1841975671.keyConcept: Nasopharynx: Exclusively respiratory chamber; lined by pseudostratified ciliated columnar (respiratory) epithelium and innervated sensory by the maxillary nerve (V2/pharyngeal nerve).

1677298647.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Vertical mucous membrane fold on the lateral nasopharyngeal wall descending from the lower part of the tubal elevation (torus tubarius) towards the lateral wall of the pharynx, containing the salpingopharyngeus muscle.
1677298647.keyConcept: Salpingopharyngeal fold: Overlies the salpingopharyngeus muscle; innervated by the pharyngeal plexus (CN X) and acts to elevate the pharynx during swallowing.

1685210862.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Funnel-shaped triangular aperture on the lateral wall of the nasopharynx situated about 1–1.5 cm posterior to the inferior nasal concha; bounded superiorly and posteriorly by the tubal elevation (torus tubarius).
1685210862.keyConcept: Pharyngeal orifice of auditory (Eustachian) tube: Connects the middle ear tympanic cavity with the nasopharynx to equalize atmospheric pressure across the tympanic membrane.

1152430832.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Prominent mucosal bulge on the lateral wall of the nasopharynx produced by the underlying cartilaginous end of the auditory (pharyngotympanic) tube, forming the superior and posterior margins of the tubal opening.
1152430832.keyConcept: Tubal elevation (torus tubarius): Cartilaginous prominence of the auditory tube; anterior attachment for salpingopharyngeus and salpingopalatine folds, situated anterior to the pharyngeal recess (fossa of Rosenmüller).

2085668788.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Prominent vertical mucosal ridge (posterior pillar of the fauces) extending from the soft palate posteroinferiorly along the lateral wall of the pharynx behind the palatine tonsil; contains the palatopharyngeus muscle.
2085668788.keyConcept: Palatopharyngeal arch: Posterior boundary of the tonsillar fossa overlying the palatopharyngeus muscle; innervated by the pharyngeal branch of the vagus nerve (CN X).

1242394192.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Distinct curved mucosal fold (anterior pillar of the fauces) descending from the oral surface of the soft palate to the lateral border of the tongue immediately anterior to the tonsillar fossa; contains the palatoglossus muscle.
1242394192.keyConcept: Palatoglossal arch: Anterior boundary of the tonsillar fossa and demarcation of the oropharyngeal isthmus; overlies palatoglossus muscle (innervated by CN X via pharyngeal plexus).

596176410.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Subepithelial aggregation of lymphoid tissue embedded in the posterior wall and roof of the nasopharynx; when pathologically enlarged in children, it is known as adenoids and can obstruct nasal breathing and auditory tube function.
596176410.keyConcept: Nasopharyngeal tonsil (adenoid): Lymphoid collection forming the superior component of Waldeyer's tonsillar ring; covered by respiratory pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium.
